pageTitle: ORBIT — Can you outplan a tiny world model?
description: Three impulses. One target. Play against a real JEPA-inspired world model, entirely in your browser.
heroBody: A tiny AI imagines 27 possible futures. You have three impulses to beat its plan. No chat. Just you, a world model, and one target.
dailyHint: The same five worlds for everyone. Choose first. See the AI’s plan afterwards.
labHint: Change the impulses. Inspect predictions. Let JEPA choose a plan. Nothing here enters the daily leaderboard.

benchmarkNote: 1,024 held-out synthetic scenes. Hit radius: 1.38 px on a 24 × 24 image. One training seed. This is not a comparison with LLMs.
learnTitle: From “what happens?” to “what should I do?”
learnIntro: A real trained neural predictor. A deliberately small, understandable world.
learn1: A frozen JEPA encoder turns two images into eight features each. It never receives the simulator’s coordinates.
learn2: A newly trained action-conditioned predictor estimates future features for all 27 three-impulse plans. It does not draw pixels.
learn3: The planner picks the final embedding closest to the goal image. Only then does the game simulate what really happens.
honesty: Not a miniature AGI. Not Meta’s V-JEPA. Not “JEPA beats LLMs”.
honestyBody: This educational JEPA-inspired system reuses a pretrained visual encoder and learns a new action predictor. The coordinate probe is supervised and used only for display and diagnostics—not plan selection. Real physics is still better at this tiny task.
